q: 1. DPC should be
explain: A Damp Proof Course (DPC) must be impervious to water, continuous to prevent gaps, and can be applied both horizontally (on walls) and vertically (to basement walls) to block moisture.

q: 2. Ceiling height of the building is the height
explain: Ceiling height specifically refers to the clear vertical distance between the finished floor level and the underside of the ceiling.

q: 3. The bearing capacity of soil depends on
explain: The grain size, shape, and grading of soil particles directly influence internal friction and cohesion, which are primary factors in determining ultimate bearing capacity.

q: 4. The foundation in a building is provided to
options: distribute the load over a large area
increase overall stability of the structure
transmit load to the bearing surface (sub soil) at a uniform rate
explain: Foundations serve multiple structural purposes: spreading concentrated loads to prevent soil failure, ensuring stability against sliding or overturning, and ensuring uniform pressure on the subsoil.

q: 5. The failure of foundation of a building is due to
options: lateral escape of the supporting material
explain: Foundation failure can occur physically (lateral escape of soil), chemically/environmentally (moisture changes causing shrinkage), or structurally (uneven settlement leading to cracks).

q: 6. The safe bearing capacity of the soil is equal to
options: ultimate bearing power / factor of safety
ultimate tensile strength / factor of safety
ultimate compressive strength / factor of safety
explain: Safe Bearing Capacity (SBC) is calculated by dividing the Ultimate Bearing Capacity (the maximum pressure soil can take before shear failure) by a Factor of Safety (usually 2.5 to 3).

q: 7. The bearing capacity of soils can be improved by
options: ramming the granular material like crushed stone in the soil
explain: Soil strength improves with depth (confinement), reduction of pore water pressure (drainage), and densification through the addition/compaction of granular materials.

q: 8. The minimum depth of foundation for buildings on clays is
explain: For clayey soils, foundations must be deep enough (typically 0.9m to 1.6m) to reach beyond the 'active zone' where seasonal moisture changes cause significant swelling and shrinkage.

q: 9. The raft foundations are generally used when the required area of footing is ........ the total area of the structure.
explain: If individual footings would cover more than 50% (one-half) of the building area, a continuous raft (mat) foundation becomes more economical and effective at reducing differential settlement.

q: 10. In combined footing
options: centre of gravity of the column loads must coincide with the centre of gravity of the footing
explain: To ensure uniform soil pressure distribution under a combined footing, the geometric center (C.G.) of the footing must align with the resultant C.G. of the two column loads.

q: 11. The best spacing of timber piles from centre to centre is
explain: For timber piles, a center-to-center spacing of 900mm is generally considered optimal to ensure the soil between piles is properly compacted without causing heave or damage to adjacent piles.

q: 12. The maximum load on the wooden pile should not exceed
explain: For standard timber piles, the safe design load is generally capped at 200 kN (approx. 20 tonnes) to prevent structural crushing of the wood fibers under sustained architectural loads.

q: 13. Pre-cast concrete piles are usually
options: plain, reinforced concrete or pre-stressed concrete
explain: Pre-cast piles must withstand significant tensile stresses during handling, transport, and driving (hammer impact). Therefore, they require either longitudinal reinforcement or pre-stressing to prevent cracking.

q: 14. The length of pre-cast concrete piles varies from
explain: Modern pre-casting and transport capabilities allow for pile lengths up to 30 meters. Lengths beyond this typically require specialized mechanical joints or cast-in-situ methods.

q: 15. According to Rankine's formula, the minimum depth of foundation should be
explain: Rankine's formula for minimum depth (h) is $h =  rac{p}{w} \left(  rac{1-\sin\phi}{1+\sin\phi} ight)^2$. It ensures the weight of the soil at that depth provides enough lateral pressure to prevent the soil under the footing from heaving.

q: 16. The minimum depth of foundation for the load bearing wall of a building is restricted to
explain: For load-bearing masonry walls in standard climatic conditions, 900 mm is the widely accepted minimum depth to ensure the foundation sits below the frost line and the zone of seasonal moisture variation.

q: 17. The dampness in a building is due to
explain: Dampness is multi-causal: it can rise from the ground (capillary action), penetrate from the roof/walls (rain), or occur due to poor material quality or lack of DPC (defective construction).

q: 18. When two or more footing are connected by a beam, is called
explain: A strap footing (or cantilever footing) consists of two individual footings connected by a structural 'strap' beam. This is often used when one footing is placed against a property line.

q: 19. In case of buildings without basement, the best position for damp-proof course (DPC) lies at
explain: For buildings without basements, the DPC is placed at the plinth level to stop capillary moisture from the ground from reaching the upper walls.

q: 20. For D.P.C. at plinth level, the commonly adopted material is
explain: In standard residential construction, a layer of rich cement concrete (typically 1:2:4) mixed with a waterproofing compound is the most common and cost-effective DPC material.

q: 21. A semi-rigid material which forms an excellent impervious layer for damp-proofing, is called
explain: Mastic asphalt is a semi-rigid mixture of asphalt, mineral filler, and fine aggregate. It is heated and poured to form a completely jointless, waterproof, and durable layer.

q: 22. The damp-proof course
options: should be of good impervious material
explain: Effective damp-proofing requires a 'barrier' approach: it must be impervious, it must be continuous (no gaps), and it must cover both vertical and horizontal paths of moisture entry.

q: 23. The construction of a temporary structure required to support an unsafe structure, is called
explain: Shoring is the provision of temporary supports (shores) to prevent the collapse of an unsafe wall or structure during repairs or nearby excavation.

q: 24. Type of foundation most suitable for bridges is
explain: Pile foundations are ideal for bridges because they can reach deep, stable soil layers or bedrock, bypassing erodible riverbed material (scour) that would undermine shallower foundations.

q: 25. A brick which is half as wide as a full brick, is called
explain: A queen closer is created by cutting a brick lengthwise into two equal halves. It is used to maintain the bond (overlap) at the end of a wall course.

q: 26. In brick masonry, for good bonding
options: all bricks need not be uniform in size
bats must be used in alternate courses only
vertical joints in alternate courses should fall in plumb
cement mortar used must have surkhi as additive
explain: Strong bonding requires that vertical joints do not align across consecutive courses. Having vertical joints 'fall in plumb' (aligning every other course) ensures maximum load distribution.

q: 27. The heading bond is usually used for
explain: A header bond (bricks laid with ends facing out) is used for walls with a thickness of one full brick (roughly 200mm) to provide better transverse strength.

q: 28. Minimum depth of foundation on clayey soils
explain: Clayey soils are highly expansive. A minimum depth of 90 cm is required to ensure the footing rests below the 'active zone' where moisture changes cause the soil to shrink or swell.

q: 29. Bearing capacity of soils cannot be improved by
explain: Watering the surface usually softens the soil and increases pore water pressure, which actually reduces the shear strength and bearing capacity rather than improving it.

q: 30. Black cotton soil is unsuitable for foundations because its
options: property to undergo a volumetric change due to variation of moisture content.
explain: Black cotton soil contains montmorillonite clay, which swells significantly when wet and shrinks/cracks when dry, leading to severe foundation movement and structural damage.

q: 31. The bearing capacity of water logged soil, may be improved by
explain: For waterlogged soil, the most effective first step is drainage. Removing excess water reduces pore pressure and increases the effective stress (and thus strength) of the soil grains.

q: 32. Dampness cause
explain: Excess moisture triggers salt migration (efflorescence), chemical breakdown of paint binders (bleaching), and creates the humid environment necessary for termite infestations.

q: 33. In horizontal D.P.C., thickness of cement concrete (1:2:4) is
explain: A standard plinth-level DPC using 1:2:4 concrete is typically 4 cm (approx. 1.5 inches) thick, providing a sufficient barrier against capillary moisture while remaining structurally sound.

q: 34. The inner section of a cavity wall, is generally known as
explain: A cavity wall consists of two separate walls (leaves) with a gap between them. The inner part is called the 'inner leaf' or 'inner leaf wall'.

q: 35. The window which is provided on a sloping roof of a building, is called
explain: A dormer window is a vertical window that projects from a sloping roof, usually including its own small roof, to provide light and ventilation to an attic or top floor.

q: 36. The window which is provided in flat roof, is known
explain: A lantern window is a glass structure installed over an opening in a flat roof to provide natural light and airflow to the space below.

q: 37. The platform at the end of a series of steps, is known as
explain: In stair design, a landing is the horizontal platform between two flights of stairs or at the top of a flight, used for resting or changing direction.

q: 38. A stair should not have pitch more than
explain: For comfort and safety, the pitch (angle of inclination) of a standard staircase should generally be between 25° and 40°. Anything steeper becomes difficult and dangerous to climb.

q: 39. A floor constructed with the 3 to 6 mm marble chips, is known
explain: Terrazzo is a composite material consisting of marble, quartz, or glass chips poured with a cementitious binder. After curing, it is ground and polished to a smooth surface.

q: 40. The process of making the background rough, before plastering, is
explain: Hacking involves roughening the surface of concrete or old masonry with a hammer or chisel to create a 'key' that allows the new plaster coat to bond mechanically.

q: 41. The type of pointing in which upper side of mortar joints is kept about 12 mm inside the face of the masonry and bottom is kept flushed with face of wall, is
explain: Struck pointing is designed to shed rainwater effectively. The slope created by recessing the top edge allows water to run off the joint rather than sitting on it.

q: 42. The process of working a flat for the finishing coat, is known
explain: Floating is the act of using a 'float' (a flat tool) to spread and level the plaster or concrete surface to create a uniform, flat plane before the final smooth troweling.

q: 43. Expansion joints in masonry walls are provided if length exceeds
explain: To prevent cracking due to thermal expansion and contraction, long masonry walls must have expansion joints at intervals, typically capped at a maximum of 40 meters.

q: 44. The nominal thickness of the brick wall in mm, is
explain: While a standard modular brick is 190mm long, the 'nominal' thickness includes the mortar joint, bringing the standard wall thickness calculation to 200mm.

q: 45. The formwork from the sides of beams can be removed only after
explain: Vertical formwork (sides of beams/columns) does not support the weight of the concrete; it only holds the shape. It can typically be removed after 24 hours (1 day).

q: 46. The formwork from the slabs excluding props, can be removed only after
explain: According to standard codes (like IS 456), slab soffit formwork can be removed after 3 days, provided the props are immediately re-fixed to support the load.

q: 47. An ordinary concrete may be made water proof by adding
explain: Products like Pudlo and Impermo are integral waterproofing admixtures, while Snowcem is a waterproof cement paint; all are used to enhance the moisture resistance of concrete structures.

q: 48. According to National Building Code, the hydrants in water mains is provided at minimum interval of
explain: Fire safety regulations in the NBC specify that fire hydrants should be placed at intervals no greater than 75 meters to ensure adequate coverage for emergency hoses.

q: 49. The foundation in which a cantilever beam is provided to join two footings, is known as
explain: A strap footing uses a cantilever 'strap' beam to connect an eccentric exterior footing to an interior footing, balancing the overturning moment caused by the edge load.

q: 50. The types of foundation used to transfer heavy load is
explain: Grillage foundations consist of tiers of steel beams (I-sections) encased in concrete. They are used specifically to spread very heavy concentrated loads from columns over a large area.

q: 51. In case of foundation on black cotton soil, the most suitable method to improve the bearing capacity of soil
explain: Because black cotton soil is chemically unstable (swelling/shrinking), the most reliable method for light structures is replacing the top 1-2 meters of soil with a non-expansive material like sand or moorum.

q: 52. In rectangular foundation of which 'B' the maximum permissible eccentricity of load is limited to
explain: To ensure no tension develops at the base of a foundation (the 'middle-third' rule), the eccentricity 'e' must not exceed B/6 for rectangular bases.

q: 53. A temporary rigid structure having platforms to enable masons to work at different stages of a building, is known as
explain: Scaffolding is a temporary structure used to support a work crew and materials to aid in the construction, maintenance, and repair of buildings.

q: 54. The arrangement made to support an unsafe structure temporarily, is known as
explain: Shoring is the process of temporarily supporting a building, vessel, structure, or trench with shores (props) when in danger of collapse or during alterations.

q: 55. The masonry with stone having chisel-dressed on all beds and joints to be true and square giving perfectly vertical & horizontal joint is called
explain: Ashlar masonry uses finely dressed stones with extremely thin joints, creating a very smooth and formal appearance compared to rubble masonry.

q: 56. Width of wall footing (according to thumb's rule) is
explain: A common rule of thumb for footing width is twice the wall thickness plus 30 cm (2t + 300mm) to ensure proper load distribution to the soil.

q: 57. The structure on which arch rests in called
explain: The abutment is the end support of an arch or bridge that resists the lateral thrust of the arch.

q: 58. Numbers of bricks required for one cubic meter masonry wall as per Nepal standard
explain: Standard practice in Nepal estimates approximately 560 bricks per cubic meter for traditional brick masonry including mortar joints.

q: 59. Brick wall could fail due to
options: rupture along a vertical joint in poorly bonded walls
explain: Brick walls can fail through various mechanisms including compression (crushing), shear, or poor interlocking (bond) between bricks.

q: 60. Cement sand mortar preferred in load bearing wall is
explain: For load-bearing walls, a 1:6 cement-to-sand ratio provides a balanced strength that allows for minor settlements without brittle failure.

q: 61. The brick laid with its breadth parallel to the face of a wall, is known as
explain: A header is a brick laid so that its end (breadth) is visible on the face of the wall.

q: 62. The main purpose of cavity wall is
explain: Cavity walls utilize an air gap to prevent moisture travel, provide thermal resistance, and act as a sound barrier.

q: 63. Cavity wall
options: prevent dampness from entering the building
have lesser dead load for given wall thickness
provide better insulation for heat & sound
explain: Cavity walls are multifunctional: they block capillary moisture, reduce building weight, and improve the indoor climate through air-gap insulation.

q: 64. Cavity wall provided with
explain: The defining feature of a cavity wall is the continuous air space (gap) between the inner and outer leaves.

q: 65. Which of the following wall is not designed for taking lateral load
explain: Gravity walls rely on their own weight to resist lateral earth pressure, but unlike buttress or counterfort walls, they aren't 'designed' with specific lateral reinforcement components.
